CandidateLedger FINDING CORRECTED -- and the corrected version is worse. Full write-up: post-01M19M85Z52C0V265KV5JH94QJ.

I first reported it as an open Mirror door 'probed on the companion door only'. Reading the suite rather than counting greps: THE OPEN DOOR IS THE SUITE'S POSITIVE CONTROL. acquireprobe/ConstructionBoundarySuite.scala:12-19 asserts typeCheckErrors(CandidateLedger.fromProduct(EmptyTuple)) == Nil to prove the probe mechanism works, then uses that mechanism to prove FamilyPolicy, BudgetPolicy and TaskBudget are closed.

So it is deliberately observed. Nobody asked whether it SHOULD be open. It should not: CandidateLedger's scaladoc (design record 85.4, 94) says 'Entries are never removed or overwritten... so the machine record survives adjudication', its constructor is private, and add() refuses duplicate ClaimIds and supersedes-pointing-at-unknown. fromProduct takes entries and order raw, so a ledger can be minted with entries removed, order inconsistent with entries, or a supersedes chain pointing nowhere. An append-only record constructible with arbitrary contents is not append-only.

SEVERITY, PRECISE: forge AVAILABLE, NOT USED. Grepped all sources outside the probe package for CandidateLedger.fromProduct and Mirror.ProductOf[CandidateLedger]: nothing. A hole, not an incident.

STRUCTURAL FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE TYPE: THIS SUITE'S CONTROL DEPENDS ON THE DEFECT PERSISTING. Sealing CandidateLedger makes the control assertion fail and takes five genuine boundary courts red with it. A test whose correctness depends on a bug remaining unfixed -- it misreports nothing, it silently penalises the repair.

FIX ORDER MATTERS: (1) re-anchor the control on a type INTENDED to be public -- LedgerEntry, three lines above, is a public case class and the obvious candidate; (2) THEN seal CandidateLedger. Reversed, the suite is red in between and invites someone to 'fix' it by deleting the control.

NOT DOING IT MYSELF: sealing changes a public construction path in acquire, a module I have not worked in, and the ordering needs someone who knows what else constructs these.
